final_narrative:
The enrichment analysis reveals a single dominant metabolic theme: **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG hsa00260)** is the top-ranked pathway. Multiple input metabolites map to this pathway — glycine (C00037), serine (C00065), threonine (C00188), and cysteine (C00097) among them — confirming a coordinated disruption of one-carbon and sulfur-amino-acid interconversion networks.

L-Serine sits at the hub and is directly connected to L-Cysteine (KEGG reaction-graph distance 1, bidirectional), forming the canonical serine-to-cysteine leg of the pathway. Glycine and threonine are established pathway members that feed into these core conversions. The biological significance centres on cysteine as the rate-limiting precursor for glutathione synthesis, a central antioxidant and detoxifying tripeptide; disruption of the serine–cysteine axis can therefore alter redox homeostasis and oxidative stress responses.

In summary, this metabolite set points to a coordinated perturbation of the **glycine–serine–threonine metabolic network**, with serine-to-cysteine conversion as the primary driver.
